title: van Aubel's theorem: equal perpendicular diagonals of square centers

problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: Formalize van Aubel's theorem: given an arbitrary planar quadrilateral, erect a square externally on each side and let P,Q,R,S be the four square centers; then the segments PR and QS are equal in length and perpendicular. Recommended route: model the four vertices as complex numbers a,b,c,d in C, write each square center via the 90-degree rotation i (center of square on edge from u to v is (u+v)/2 + i*(v-u)/2), and prove (R - P) = i*(S - Q) by a direct ring computation over C; this single identity yields both |PR| = |QS| and PR perpendicular to QS. Not a named Mathlib result.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED & BUILD-VERIFIED. The complex-number formalization (shipped build-pending in #24989) compiles clean in Docker: 0 sorry, 0 axiom, 3 theorems. squareCenter u v = (u+v)/2 + I*(v-u)/2; the single ring identity vanAubel_key : R-P = I*(S-Q) gives both equal-length (norm_mul + norm_I) and perpendicular (mul_conj, real part 0) diagonals.
insights: The entire theorem collapses to one linear_combination over C using Complex.I_sq (I^2=-1); erecting squares via the +90 rotation i*(v-u) makes R-P = i*(S-Q) an exact algebraic identity, so equal length and perpendicularity are both free.
Perpendicularity is cleanly encoded as ((R-P) * conj(S-Q)).re = 0 (vanishing Euclidean inner product), discharged by Complex.mul_conj + the real part of a purely-imaginary number.
Confirmed the build-pending entry (#24989) is genuinely verified in Docker under current Mathlib; also removed an unused simp argument (Complex.I_mul_re) flagged by the unusedSimpArgs linter.
